pr.title: Install the plugins Projector depends on before a Claude CI review, so the review-pr skill loads
pr.head: 98f788d6d5363539a2a7379b19f9e311daa0b574

summary: Projector can review pull requests in GitHub Actions: its actions/review action installs an agent's CLI on the runner and has it run Projector's review-pr skill. For Claude, the action gives Claude Code Projector's source as a plugin with --plugin-dir, and the plugin supplies the skill.

Projector's plugin manifest, .claude-plugin/plugin.json, lists gh-stack as a dependency, and Claude Code loads no plugin whose dependency is missing. The runner had no gh-stack, so the plugin never loaded and the agent never had the skill. Most agents found the skill's files and followed them anyway. One didn't, published no verdict, and failed its job.

This change adds two commands to the action's install step. They register Projector's own source tree as a plugin marketplace, a catalogue of plugins that .claude-plugin/marketplace.json describes, and install gh-stack from it at the commit the catalogue pins. A test runs the install step against fake npm and claude commands, and the CI review documentation describes the step.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Marketplace: a catalogue of Claude Code plugins. Projector's lists Projector itself and gh-stack, pinned to a tag and commit.
  • Dependency: a plugin another plugin's manifest names. Claude Code refuses to load the dependent plugin until the dependency is installed.
  • Persistent runner: a self-hosted runner that keeps its files, ~/.claude included, from one job to the next.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html: The review of 98f788d requests changes with one finding: on a persistent runner, claude plugin install leaves an older gh-stack in place after a Projector upgrade changes the pin.

groups.title: Install the dependencies before the review
groups.kicker: The action's install step adds the marketplace and installs gh-stack
intro: Right after the Claude Code CLI is installed, the action registers $PROJECTOR_ROOT, the Projector source tree the action runs from, as a marketplace. It then installs gh-stack@projector, meaning the gh-stack plugin from the marketplace named projector. With the dependency installed, the plugin that --plugin-dir passes loads, and with it the review-pr skill.
The Codex path needs nothing like this: the action links Projector's skills straight into the Codex home, and Codex checks no dependencies.

files.note: Two new commands in the claude branch of the Install the agent step.

checks.text: In a throwaway Claude Code 2.1.327 config, both commands exit 0 when run a second time, and adding the marketplace again from another path repoints it and also exits 0. This review itself ran with the plugin loaded.

Open finding: once gh-stack is installed, install keeps it at the old version even after a Projector upgrade changes the pin, so a persistent runner keeps the old gh-stack. Running claude plugin update gh-stack@projector after the install brings it to the pin.

groups.title: Test and documentation
groups.kicker: A test of the install step's commands, and a sentence in the CI review guide
intro: The new test runs the action's install step with fake npm and claude commands that log how they're called. It checks that the step adds the marketplace before installing, and that it installs each dependency the manifest names from a marketplace that carries that dependency. The existing helper's fake npm now leaves a fake agent CLI behind, so the new claude plugin calls in later steps have something to run.

files.note: Describes the new step under what each review job does.
